source: Hitopadesha (Narayana), Prastāvikā (introduction), verse 0.36: udyamena hi sidhyanti kāryāṇi na manorathaiḥ / nahi suptasya siṃhasya praviśanti mukhe mṛgāḥ. Text: GRETIL, Narayana: Hitopadesa v1.1 (input J. Brzezinski, rev. U. Stiehl), read 2026-11-24. Frame: King Sudarśana of Pāṭaliputra hands his sons to Viṣṇuśarman for teaching (same text).

shots.art: A lone young student sits on a high rock under a vast swirling dusk sky, seen from behind, one arm raised toward a single bright star; a small clay oil lamp burns on the rock beside them; far below, misty hills.
Before dawn, a student seen from behind writing at a small wooden desk by an open window; a brass oil lamp, a stack of books, a cup of tea; violet sky and the last stars outside.
A lion asleep and peaceful under a great banyan tree at dusk; at a safe distance a deer grazes, calm and untouched, in tall golden grass. Gentle storybook mood, nothing threatening.
hi: सोते हुए शेर के मुँह में

shots.art: An old palm-leaf manuscript tied with cord lies open on a low wooden stand beside an oil lamp in a quiet courtyard; around it, small storybook animals: a crow on the wall, a tortoise, a mouse, a deer at the doorway.
en: told to teach a king's sons.
hi: जो राजकुमारों को सिखाने के लिए कही गई।

shots.art: A long path winds up a hillside toward a rising sun; one small traveller with a cloth bag walks up it, seen from behind; fields and a river far below.
en: Use it in an Essay on hard work,
hi: या GS4 में लगन पर, इसे लिखिए।
